posts.caption:
**Crawling through five hundred yards of toxic sewage in Shawshank, he headlined the highest-rated movie in history.**

Born October 16, 1958, in West Covina, California, and raised in Greenwich Village, today Timothy Francis Robbins turns **68**.

The son of a folk musician, Tim grew up handing out flyers and performing street theater, moving to Los Angeles with little money and facing endless pilot rejections.

While 1980s studios sought musclebound action heroes, Tim trusted an unorthodox instinct: towering six-foot-five intellectual stillness and moral depth.

After breakout turns in *Bull Durham* and *The Player*, he starred as wrongfully convicted banker Andy Dufresne in 1994's *The Shawshank Redemption*, which bombed at the box office before becoming the undisputed number-one rated movie on IMDb.

He earned an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for *Mystic River* while writing and directing the searing death row masterpiece *Dead Man Walking*.

At 68, Tim Robbins stands as an uncompromising titan of dramatic integrity who proved hope is a good thing that never dies.

**Where did Tim Robbins deliver his greatest performance: Andy Dufresne in Shawshank or Dave Boyle in Mystic River? Vote below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Tim Robbins's Shawshank Redemption sewage scene...**

* The muddy stream Andy Dufresne crawls through to escape Shawshank was actually real toxic agricultural runoff, which tested dangerously high for bacteria right before filming.
* He spent days locked alone in solitary confinement at the abandoned Ohio State Reformatory to prepare mentally for the psychological isolation of Andy Dufresne.

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: When The Shawshank Redemption premiered in theaters, it was a box-office failure that barely made back its budget. Yet Tim Robbins brought such profound quiet hope to Andy Dufresne that it became the highest-rated film in cinema history before he won an Oscar for Mystic River. Happy sixty-eighth birthday to a monumental Hollywood actor and director. What is your all-time favorite movie of his?
posts.reel_caption: The Shawshank Redemption flopped in theaters before becoming the highest-rated movie in history. What is your favorite Tim Robbins performance? #TimRobbins #ShawshankRedemption #MysticRiver #BullDurham #BornToday

posts.caption:
**Fleeing wartime London bombs, she arrived in America with one suitcase and became television's greatest detective.**

Born October 16, 1925, in Regent's Park, London, today Dame Angela Brigid Lansbury would have celebrated her **101st** milestone.

Fleeing the Blitz bombings with her mother in 1940, Angela worked wrapping packages in a department store before signing with MGM at age seventeen.

She scored Oscar nominations for her first two films, *Gaslight* and *The Picture of Dorian Gray*, and terrified audiences in *The Manchurian Candidate*.

When Hollywood relegated mature actresses to the background, Angela trusted an unorthodox instinct: boundless warmth, theater vitality, and sharp intellect.

She conquered Broadway with five Tony Awards, voiced the beloved Mrs. Potts in Disney's *Beauty and the Beast*, and anchored *Murder, She Wrote* for 264 episodes as mystery writer Jessica Fletcher.

Beloved across four generations, Dame Angela Lansbury remains the ultimate symbol of British-American grace, longevity, and warmth.

**What brings back the best memories: watching Murder, She Wrote on Sunday nights or singing along with Mrs. Potts in Beauty and the Beast? Share below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind Angela Lansbury's iconic Beauty and the Beast recording...**

* Angela recorded the legendary title song 'Beauty and the Beast' in just one single take after traveling all night following a bomb threat on her flight.
* Across twelve seasons of *Murder, She Wrote*, Angela was nominated for eighteen Primetime Emmy Awards, setting a historic television record.

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: Escaping the London Blitz bombings as a teenager, Angela Lansbury arrived in America and conquered stage and screen for eight decades. From her chilling Oscar-nominated turn in The Manchurian Candidate to singing Tale As Old As Time in Beauty and the Beast and solving crimes as Jessica Fletcher, she was pure magic. Remembering an irreplaceable legend on her birthday. What was your favorite role of hers?
posts.reel_caption: Fleeing Blitz bombs with one suitcase, Angela Lansbury earned six Tony Awards and anchored Murder, She Wrote for twelve seasons. What is your favorite Angela Lansbury memory? #AngelaLansbury #MurderSheWrote #BeautyAndTheBeast #BornToday

posts.caption:
**Working at a gas station to buy a guitar, he dropped out of college to become a seven-time Grammy-winning icon.**

Born October 16, 1977, in Bridgeport, Connecticut, today John Clayton Mayer turns **49**, celebrated as one of modern music's finest guitarists.

Becoming obsessed with Stevie Ray Vaughan as a teenager, John practiced until his fingers bled, dropping out of Berklee College of Music to busk in Atlanta coffeehouses.

While radio in the 2000s favored manufactured pop, John trusted an unorthodox instinct: soulful acoustic songwriting and vintage blues chops.

His breakout albums *Room for Squares* and *Heavier Things* made him an international superstar, before his 2006 masterpiece *Continuum* cemented his standing among guitar gods alongside Eric Clapton and B.B. King.

When severe granuloma throat surgery silenced his singing voice for months in 2011, John adapted, joining surviving members of the Grateful Dead to anchor Dead & Company.

At 49, John Mayer has navigated fame, reinvention, and pure musicianship to stand as an enduring guitar icon.

**Which John Mayer album is your absolute favorite: Continuum, Room for Squares, or Born and Raised? Drop your thoughts below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind John Mayer's Continuum guitar tone...**

* John recorded the Grammy-winning hit 'Gravity' completely live in the studio with the John Mayer Trio, capturing the raw emotional solo in just one continuous take.
* When vocal cord granulomas threatened to permanently destroy his singing voice in 2011, he underwent high-risk surgery and couldn't speak for months.

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: Working at a gas station to buy his first guitar, John Mayer practiced obsessively until his fingers bled. Dropping out of music school, he blended pop songwriting with blistering blues guitar to win seven Grammy Awards and headline stadiums with Dead and Company. Happy forty-ninth birthday to one of the greatest modern guitar heroes. What is your absolute favorite John Mayer song of all time?
